dū^plĭcārĭus ,
			ii, m.
		duplex, 
I.a soldier who receives double pay as a reward,
				Varr. L. L. 5, § 90
			Müll.; Liv. 2, 59 fin.;
					Inscr. Orell. 3533;
			4994 (cf. Caes. B. C. 3, 53 fin.; Liv. 7, 37; and 24, 47); 
				“also written DUPLICIARIUS,”
				 Inscr. Orell. 3534
			; see also duplaris.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
